reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Mondays used to feel like a punishment. Sunday night was for damage assessment — what did I say, who did I owe an apology to, could I actually make it through a full workweek without unraveling by Wednesday. The dread was so familiar I stopped noticing it was there. I thought that low hum of anxiety was just what being an adult felt like.

It isn't. That hum belonged to the drinking. When it lifted, what I found underneath wasn't some cinematic bliss — it was just a normal Monday. Coffee that tastes like coffee. A commute I can actually be present for. Emails I can respond to without rehearsing an excuse. The ordinary stopped being something I had to survive and started being something I could live inside.

Durant's line gets used a lot, but it lands different in sobriety. You don't become someone you can live with in a single dramatic moment. You become that person by making the bed, showing up to the meeting, calling the friend back, going to bed at a reasonable hour on a Sunday. The small repeated acts are the whole thing. A Monday you don't have to hide from isn't a small win — it's the actual life you were told didn't exist for people like you. It was always here. You just had to be sober enough to walk into it.
reflection.meditation: Sit for two minutes before the day starts. Notice: no dread, or less dread. Whatever's there, let it be there without needing to fix it.

affirmations: I am building a life through small repeated choices, not grand gestures.
Today I can meet an ordinary Monday without needing to escape it.
I am becoming someone I actually want to spend the day with.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Monday morning I don't have to piece back together. Grateful for the version of me that kept showing up on the days it felt pointless, because he's the reason today is quiet in the best way. Grateful for coffee, for a clear head, for work I can actually do, for people who know my real name and my real story.
gratitude.closing: One more day, one more Monday, one foot in front of the other.
